title: Etale descent of local module flatifications
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, $f:X\to S$ a morphism of schemes, $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $U\subset S$ a quasi-compact open. Suppose a finite family of diagrams $X_i\xrightarrow{j_i}X$, $X_i\to S_i\xrightarrow{e_i}S$ commutes with $f$. Assume each $e_i$ is quasi-compact and etale, $S=\bigcup_i e_i(S_i)$, each $j_i$ is etale, and $X=\bigcup_i j_i(X_i)$. Suppose for each $i$ there is an $e_i^{-1}(U)$-admissible blowup $S_i^*\to S_i$ such that the module strict transform of $j_i^*\mathcal F$ on $X_i\times_{S_i}S_i^*$ is flat over $S_i^*$. Then there is a $U$-admissible blowup $S^b\to S$ such that the module strict transform of $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S^b$. Admissibility and module strict transform have the meanings of [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], [def-trf-module-strict-transform]; etale is as in [def-weil-etale-morphism].

proof.text: Replace the diagrams by their finite affine refinement (first clause), relabelling $W_r,Y_r$ as $S_i,X_i$; now all $S_i$ are qcqs. Choose a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K$ with $V(\mathcal K)=S\setminus U$ and blow it up. Principalization makes its extension an effective Cartier ideal. The calculus preserves qcqs and quasi-coherence; the stability lemma preserves all local-flatification hypotheses. Choose finitely many affine opens $V_\alpha$ trivializing the Cartier ideal: on each, $U=D(a_\alpha)$ with $a_\alpha$ a nonzerodivisor. A finite subcover exists by quasi-compactness. Write $S_1$ for this base, $X_1=X\times_SS_1$, and $\mathcal F_1$ for its transform on $X_1$.

Restrict the diagrams to $V_\alpha$. The inclusions of the inverse images of $V_\alpha$ are open immersions, hence etale and so flat. Etale covering base change preserves both covering families; qc base change preserves quasi-compactness of the base maps, and flat pullback of strict transforms preserves the given local flatifications. Apply the affine-refinement lemma (second clause) over $V_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}A_\alpha$. It gives finite affine charts $W_r$, still covering both targets, with centres $\mathcal J_r$ and base ideals $I_r$ satisfying $I_r\mathcal O_{W_r}=\mathcal J_r\mathcal J'_r$ and $V(I_r)\subset V(a_\alpha)$.

Apply product-centre domination to the ideals $I_r$ on this affine chart. The maps from Step 2 are flat because they are etale. It gives a $(U\cap V_\alpha)$-admissible product blowup $B_\alpha\to V_\alpha$ whose transform of $\mathcal F_1$ pulls back on each $Y_r\times_{V_\alpha}B_\alpha$ to a module flat over $W_r\times_{V_\alpha}B_\alpha$.

Write $Z=X_1\times_{S_1}B_\alpha$ and $Z_r=Y_r\times_{V_\alpha}B_\alpha$. Etale-cover base change makes $Z_r\to Z$ a jointly surjective flat family and $W_r\times_{V_\alpha}B_\alpha\to B_\alpha$ flat. At $z_r\in Z_r$, write $t_r$ and $b$ for its images in these two bases. Step 3 gives flatness of the pulled-back module stalk over $\mathcal O_{W_r\times_{V_\alpha}B_\alpha,t_r}$. This ring is flat over $\mathcal O_{B_\alpha,b}$; module-flatness transitivity therefore gives flatness over the latter ring. The stalkwise definition and relative-flatness source descent now give flatness of the transform on $Z$ over $B_\alpha$.

Apply finite Zariski gluing to the flatifications $B_\alpha\to V_\alpha$: it extends their centres and blows up their product on $S_1$, obtaining a flat transform everywhere. Compose with $S_1\to S$ using calculus (1). This is $U$-admissible and its transform is the successive flat transform, as required. Empty schemes give vacuous flatness and unit empty products; if $U=S$, admissible centres are unit ideals and Step 4 gives flatness without modification.

Re-split note: old steps 1+5 become affine-refinement, 2+3 become blowup-stability, 6+7 become factorized-centres-product-transform and 9 becomes zariski-gluing. Old steps 4, 8 and 10 are item steps 1, 4 and 5, each written out in full. Nothing is dropped, and no new node restates the item. Each child is true: the refinement uses 0813 on étale A->B with J unit on D(a), so V(J) is inside V(aB); stability uses flat base change and the two-ideal blowup, and the strict transform depends only on the support; the product node's support identity V(J K)=V(J) ∪ c(V(KO)) holds because c is an isomorphism off V(J), even when c is not surjective; gluing extends the ideal glued over U ∪ V_alpha to the qcqs base.
